0.long_answer: The infection that typically causes chorioretinitis, where the most common symptom is decreased visual acuity in one eye, is ocular toxoplasmosis. This condition is caused by the protozoan parasite Toxoplasma gondii. Toxoplasmosis is the most common cause of infections of the posterior segment of the eye. The classic presentation includes a unilateral decrease in visual acuity, often with a focal white retinitis and associated inflammation, described as a "headlight-in-fog" appearance on ophthalmic examination. In congenital cases, the disease may be bilateral, but among acquired cases, a unilateral decrease in vision is most common.
